title: Learning When Diffusion Language Models Should Regenerate
why_read: A focused technical fix for a known weakness in diffusion language models, showing a learned verifier can meaningfully improve accuracy on reasoning tasks at a measured compute cost.
analysis: Diffusion language models can revisit and remask parts of their generated text to fix mistakes, but the paper shows that simple token confidence often fails to flag actual errors, and naive remasking of an isolated mistake tends to just regenerate the same mistake because the surrounding context stays fixed. The proposed method, DiVR, trains a separate verifier to predict whether a partially generated sequence will end up correct, and uses that signal to decide when to regenerate a block and which candidate to keep. On reasoning benchmarks it raises accuracy substantially over the base model at a lower computational overhead than comparable search-based approaches. This is a solid, specific contribution to improving diffusion-based text generation, a less mature alternative to standard autoregressive LLMs.
